The three articles you posted here (1 in the OP and 2 in a comment) are really interesting. When you really read them they have a couple really odd features. Before getting to them, though, my thoughts on the two countries:

I am personally of the opinion that Hungary is a bit authoritarian and I don't share the unquestioning love and support of Orban and their government that many on Voat do. But I also don't have specific reasons to distrust them or to overstate my suspicions on possible corruption there.

I really have very little opinion on Finland at all. I suspect they are more authoritarian than my American preferences lead me to like. They are proud members of the EU and have the typical European mindset which assumes the government is separate from and above the people, like a benevolent parent, not like a subservient collective entity which should be under the people's control.

So back to the articles. First, for all the complaints against Hnugary being authoritiarian and not having a strong rule of law, they actually contain no evidence for this at all. They basically simply insult them as being worried about losing EU subsidies and not being as subservient to the EU as good little minions should be.

Second, Hungary's charge against Finland is that they do not have strong rule of law, an independent judiciary, etc. To combat this claim, the articles contain no contrary facts to the charges. Instead two of them just say that the NGO, Reporters San Frontières, ranks Finland really high in terms of press freedom. Leaving aside the validity of those rankings, this is a complete non sequitur anyway. It is as though they couldn't actually refute the legal system point so they engaged in diversion and talked about press freedoms.

Lastly, knowing the different speech laws in Europe and elsewhere, that map of press freedoms is very hard to believe. Germany is among the most free even though they will throw people in prison for what they say? That being the case, I have no reason to trust their use of the rankings to support Finland is meaningful in any way.
